name: bare-stow
description: Module bundling and harness generation for Bare

extraSections.heading: Targets
extraSections.body:
- `bare-sidecar` runs the bundle in a separate process using <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-sidecar>, with the `javascript`, `python`, and `swift` languages on desktop. In JavaScript and Python, `start()` also accepts the options of `bare-sidecar`.
- `bare-worker` runs the bundle in a thread of a Bare host using <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-worker>, with the `javascript` language.
- `bare-kit` runs the bundle in a worklet using <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-kit>, with the `swift` language on macOS and iOS and the `kotlin` language on Android and the JVM. `start()` also accepts the options of the worklet and returns it alongside `ipc`, and on Android takes the `Context` first. In Kotlin, the worklet is closed once it exits, so it needs no closing of its own, and in Swift it's released with its last reference. Native addons are linked with <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-link> and declared in the manifest, and assets are written next to the bundle. With the target option `linking` set to `'app'`, both are left to `link()` instead. On the JVM, addons and assets are written next to the bundle as files, which `start()` extracts along with the bundle to a temporary directory, so `linking` must be `'package'`.

extraSections.heading: Linking
extraSections.body:
A target may leave addons and assets to the application, so that bundles sharing them don't each bring a copy. For `bare-kit`, stow each bundle with the target option `linking` set to `'app'`:

```console
$ bare-stow pack --target bare-kit --target-option linking=app --language swift --out ./ios/Core ./core.js
```

`link()` then links the addons and assets of all bundles once, into a package the application depends on:

```js
const entries = [new URL('file:///app/core.js'), new URL('file:///app/push.js')]
const out = new URL('file:///app/ios/BareKitAddons/')

for await (const artifact of stow.link(entries, 'bare-kit', out, { language: 'swift' })) {
  console.log(artifact.url.href)
}
```

The language lays out the package and the target adds what loads the addons. For `bare-kit`, that's `bare-kit-swift` or `bare-kit-kotlin`. The assets go in a folder named by `stow.resources`, listed in a file of the same name with the `.assets` extension, which a Swift application copies into its bundle. `link()` takes the same options as `stow()`, except `client` and `base`.

extraSections.heading: Languages
extraSections.body:
The harness is generated in one of these languages, selected with `language` and configured with `languageOptions`:

- `javascript` writes an npm package. The `module` option is either `'esm'`, the default, or `'cjs'`.
- `kotlin` writes a Gradle module. The `package` option names the package of the generated code and is required. The `platform` option is either `'android'`, the default, for an Android library module, or `'jvm'` for a Kotlin/JVM library module on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The dependencies are published to JitPack (<https://jitpack.io>), so add it to the repositories of the application.
- `python` writes a Python package.
- `swift` writes a Swift package.

For example, with an RPC client and server:

```console
$ bare-stow pack --target bare-sidecar --language python --client bare-rpc --server bare-rpc --out ./my-core ./core.js
```

```python
import asyncio

import my_core


async def main():
    ipc, rpc = await my_core.start(
        handlers=lambda router: router.on_request(2, lambda req: b"hello")
    )

    await rpc.request(1, b"ping")
    await ipc.terminate()


asyncio.run(main())
```

With an RPC client, `start()` takes the handlers for the requests and events of the bundle, so that they are registered before the bundle can send any.

extraSections.heading: Protocol
extraSections.body:
The harness and the bundle multiplex a control channel and the user data over a single duplex stream. The `ipc` returned from `start()` is a duplex stream of the user data, so RPC libraries such as `bare-rpc` bind to it like any other stream. Embedders bringing their own transport can use the protocol directly:

- <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-protocol> implements the framing.
- <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-host> implements the host side and documents `ipc`, with <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-host-kotlin>, <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-host-python>, and <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-host-swift> for the other languages.
- <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-runtime> implements the bundle side.

extraSections.heading: Providers
extraSections.body: Languages, targets, and RPC libraries are providers that may live outside `bare-stow`. `stow()` and `link()` accept a provider object in place of a name, and names other than the built-in ones are resolved through `resolveLanguage`, `resolveTarget`, and `resolveRPC`. For example, <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stow-target-react-native> is a target for React Native. Targets and RPC libraries generate code for each language they list under `languages`, and providers without an entry for the language of the harness are rejected. Targets may also take options, given as `targetOptions`. The server side of an RPC library is always generated as JavaScript, as the bundle runs in Bare. See `index.d.ts` for the interfaces.

extraSections.heading: CLI
extraSections.body:
#### `bare-stow pack [flags] <entry>`

Stow the module graph rooted at `<entry>` into the directory given by `--out`.

```console
--target <name>
--target-option <key=value>
--language <name>
--language-option <key=value>
--client <name>
--server <name>
--base <path>
--out|-o <path>
--builtins <path>
--imports <path>
--defer <specifier>
--host <name>
--help|-h
```

#### `bare-stow link [flags] <entry...>`

Link the addons and assets of the module graphs rooted at each `<entry>` into the package given by `--out`.

```console
--target <name>
--target-option <key=value>
--language <name>
--language-option <key=value>
--server <name>
--out|-o <path>
--builtins <path>
--imports <path>
--defer <specifier>
--host <name>
--help|-h
```

`--target`, `--language`, `--client`, and `--server` take a built-in name, the name of a `bare-stow-target-<name>`, `bare-stow-language-<name>`, or `bare-stow-rpc-<name>` package, or a module specifier, resolved from the working directory. `--target-option`, `--language-option`, `--defer`, and `--host` may be passed multiple times. `--host` must name hosts the target supports, and defaults to all of them.

`--builtins` and `--imports` are paths to JavaScript or JSON files exporting a list of builtin modules and a map of import overrides, which are forwarded to `bare-pack`.

exports.name: stow
signatures: stow(entry: URL | string, target: Target | TargetName, out: URL | string, opts?: StowOptions): AsyncGenerator<StowArtifact>
exports.description:
Bundle the module graph rooted at `entry` for `target`, writing a harness package plus bundle to
`out`.

params.name: entry
params.description: The entry module to bundle, as a `file:` URL or path string.

params.name: target
params.description:
The bundling target: a `Target` object, or a target name resolved to one (the
built-in `bare-kit`, `bare-sidecar`, and `bare-worker`, or a `bare-stow-target-<name>` package).

params.name: out
params.description: The directory to write the harness package to, as a `file:` URL or path string.

params.name: opts
params.description: Options; see [`StowOptions`](#stowoptions).

returns.description:
An async generator that yields each written artifact's `url` as it is produced: any
addons linked into the package, the harness and its type declaration, the RPC client and its type
declaration, the package manifest, the bundle along with its `base`, and then any assets of a
linked bundle, any offloaded addon or asset files, and the listing of those files.

throws.condition: A language option is unknown or invalid, or `out` is not valid as a package.
The target or an RPC library does not support the language.
A host in `opts.hosts` is not supported by the resolved target in the language.

members.name: stow.LanguageOptions
members.description:
Options resolved by a language from those given and passed to every provider generating code in
that language. A target may pin some of them through `TargetLanguage.options`.

members.name: stow.link
signatures: stow.link(entries: URL | string | (URL | string)[], target: Target | TargetName, out: URL | string, opts?: LinkOptions): AsyncGenerator<StowArtifact>
members.description:
Link the addons and assets of the graphs rooted at `entries` into a package at `out`, once for
an application. The language lays out the package and the target adds what loads the addons.

params.name: entries
params.description: The entry modules of the graphs, as `file:` URLs or path strings.

params.name: target
params.description: The target the graphs are stowed for, or its name.

params.name: out
params.description: The directory to write the package to, as a `file:` URL or path string.

params.name: opts
params.description: Options; see [`LinkOptions`](#linkoptions).

returns.description:
An async generator that yields the `url` of each linked addon and asset, and then of the
module and manifest of the package.

throws.condition: `entries` is empty, or the `target` or `out` argument is missing.
The target does not link addons, or does not support linking for the language.
The language does not support linked addons or assets.
Two different assets would link to the same path.

members.name: defaultType
members.description:
The type to assume for a module that has no type of its own, such as one
with an ambiguous extension or a `data:` URL that no import reaches. See
`constants` for possible values.

members.name: deferUnresolved
members.description:
Record a specifier that resolves nowhere under `deferredProtocol` rather
than throwing, leaving it for whoever names it to resolve when they get
there. Only for callers that reach a resolver again, such as a module
system; a tool that only links wants the error.

An addon resolved for several `hosts` must resolve for each of the native
ones, as WebAssembly hosts are only a fallback. A host that it resolves
nothing for is unresolved, and is deferred under its own conditions or
else fails with `ADDON_NOT_FOUND`.

members.name: importType
members.description:
The type of the import that led to the entry. A JavaScript `data:` URL
takes its type from this: `REQUIRE` means a script and `IMPORT` a module,
while `IMPORT | DYNAMIC` could mean either and so needs a `type`
attribute.

members.description: The language of the harness (or its name). Defaults to `javascript`.

members.name: languageOptions
members.description: The options given to the language, such as `{ module: 'cjs' }` for `javascript`.

members.name: listPrefix
members.description: List the files under the prefix `url`. Defaults to listing the directory.

members.name: mount
members.description:
The URL the entry is mounted at when it is a bundle, for consumers that
load it with an explicit mount. The addons and assets it declares resolve
relative to this. Defaults to the URL of the entry itself.
